title: Lifting a proper clopen fibre part of a separated finite-type scheme over a henselian pair
statement: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] be a separated morphism of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $X_0=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, the base change [def-pc-base-change]. If $Y\subseteq X_0$ is an open and closed subscheme whose structure morphism $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], then there is an open and closed subscheme $W\subseteq X$, proper over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, such that $W\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)=Y$ as subschemes of $X_0$. An open and closed subscheme carries the structure sheaf restricted from the ambient scheme. The ambient scheme $X$ is not assumed proper, Noetherian or of finite presentation.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. The affine scheme $S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: apply [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] to its identity morphism, which is quasi-compact and separated. The given $f:X\to S$ is separated and of finite type, so [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}S$. By [def-nagata-compactification] and [def-nagata-compactifiable], $j$ is an open immersion, $p$ is proper, and $p\circ j=f$. Here we use Nagata as the existing general compactification tool in place of the Chow reduction of 0CT9; the boundary argument is the second paragraph of that proof.

source.place: Tag 0CT9, lemma-split-off-proper-part-henselian, second reduction paragraph (proper compactification and removal of its boundary).

proof.text: Base change gives an open immersion $j_0:X_0\hookrightarrow\overline X_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. Thus $Y$ identifies with an open subscheme $Y^c=j_0(Y)$ of $\overline X_0$. The latter is proper, hence separated, over $S_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] and [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Since $Y\to S_0$ is proper by hypothesis, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] makes $Y\to\overline X_0$ proper. Its image is closed: universal closedness applied to the identity base change is closedness, and the entire domain is closed in itself. Consequently $Y^c$ is open and closed in $\overline X_0$, with the restricted structure sheaf.

source.place: Tag 0CT9, lemma-split-off-proper-part-henselian, second reduction paragraph (proper compactification and removal of its boundary).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-clopen-restriction] to the proper scheme $\overline X\to S$ and the same henselian pair $(A,I)$. Its surjectivity assertion gives a clopen subset $\overline W\subseteq\overline X$ whose restriction to $\overline X_0$ is $Y^c$. Give it the restricted structure sheaf. Its inclusion is a closed immersion: locally on the ambient scheme the sheaf map is the identity on $\overline W$ and the map to zero on its open complement, hence is surjective. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], $\overline W\to S$ is proper. By open-immersion base change [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], its closed fibre is the open subscheme on $Y^c$, so $\overline W_0=Y^c$ as subschemes, not merely as underlying subsets.

source.place: Tag 0CT9, lemma-split-off-proper-part-henselian, second reduction paragraph (proper compactification and removal of its boundary).

proof.text: The boundary $T=\overline W\setminus j(X)$ is closed in $\overline W$, since $j(X)$ is open, and is disjoint from $\overline W_0=Y^c\subseteq j_0(X_0)$. If $t\in T$, its closure $C=\overline{\{t\}}$ in $\overline W$ is nonempty, closed, irreducible and contained in $T$. Indeed, if two relatively closed subsets cover $C$, one contains $t$ and therefore its closure $C$. Apply the irreducible-closed-subset assertion of [lemma-weil-pbc-stein-connectedness] to the proper scheme $\overline W\to S$: it says $C$ meets its closed fibre in a nonempty connected subset. This contradicts $T\cap\overline W_0=\varnothing$. Hence $T=\varnothing$ and $\overline W\subseteq j(X)$. No local, Noetherian or completeness assumption on $A$ was used.

source.place: Tag 0CT9, lemma-split-off-proper-part-henselian, second reduction paragraph (proper compactification and removal of its boundary).

proof.text: Let $W=j^{-1}(\overline W)$ with the restricted structure sheaf. It is open and closed in $X$ by continuity, and the open immersion $j$ restricts to an isomorphism $W\simeq\overline W$ by [def-weil-open-immersion], since Step 4 gives its entire image. Thus $W\to S$ is proper, being identified with $\overline W\to S$. Base change of this restriction, or equivalently taking the inverse image under $j_0$, gives $W_0=j_0^{-1}(\overline W_0)=j_0^{-1}(j_0(Y))=Y$ as open subschemes of $X_0$. Equality of their restricted structure sheaves follows from the open-immersion description in [def-weil-open-immersion] and its base-change assertion [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. This proves the required equality of subschemes.

lean.statement: theorem Scheme.exists_proper_clopen_of_henselianPair {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) [HenselianRing A I] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (Y : (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)))).Opens) (hY : IsClosed (Y : Set ↥(pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)))))) [IsProper (Y.ι ≫ pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))))] : ∃ W : X.Opens, IsClosed (W : Set X) ∧ IsProper (W.ι ≫ f) ∧ (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)))) ⁻¹ᵁ W = Y

reviewed_lean.note: Stacks 0CT9 checked clause by clause: HenselianRing A I (pair notion); IsSeparated + LocallyOfFiniteType + QuasiCompact f = recorded finite type; closed fibre = pullback f (Spec.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)); Y an open of X_0 with IsClosed and IsProper (Y.ι ≫ pullback.snd); conclusion ∃ W : X.Opens, closed, IsProper (W.ι ≫ f), pullback.fst ⁻¹ᵁ W = Y (equality of open subschemes via isPullback_morphismRestrict). No extra assumptions; universe u standard. Edge cases Y=∅, X=∅, A=0, I=0, non-proper X all covered.
